To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
liver surgery is a curative treatment for liver metastasis from breast cancer.
surgical resection of liver tumors from breast cancer can be performed safely with low morbidity and mortality rates.
the surgical resection of liver lesions from breast cancer patients is associated with a 5 year survival of about 40%, with a median overall survival of about 30 months.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the surgical resection of liver tumors.
the role of surgery of liver metastases of breast cancer.
the role of surgical resection of liver secondaries in breast cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
liver metastasis from breast cancer should be considered as a potentially resectable disease.
surgical treatment of liver metastasis from breast cancer should not be denied to any patient who is a candidate.
liver resection for liver-only metastases from breast carcinoma is indicated in patients with good performance status and no extrahepatic disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver is a sanctuary for breast cancer metastases.
liver resection for metastasis from breast cancer should be considered in patients with a good performance status, no extrahepatic metastasis, and a limited disease.
the liver resection of metastatic breast cancer is an efficient procedure with an acceptable risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hepatic surgery is the treatment of choice in patients with a limited number of liver metastases.
surgical resection of hepatic metastasis from breast cancer is a valid treatment option.
the prognosis of breast cancer patients with liver metastases is poor.
